metadata.title: Large graphs for the degree–diameter problem: n(5,7) ≥ 5894, n(6,3) ≥ 120, n(7,4) ≥ 684, n(7,5) ≥ 2758, n(13,3) ≥ 952, n(14,3) ≥ 1094, n(14,4) ≥ 8303
metadata.description:
Version 5. Adds two non-isomorphic 13-regular graphs of diameter 3 on 952 vertices: n(13,3) ≥ 952. The current table entry is 873 (Dharunish Yugeswardeenoo, 7 October 2026), obtained by a different construction; our earlier (13,3) graph on 868 vertices is described below. Construction: each vertex of Rishabh Rajiv's (6,3) graph on 119 vertices (his entry in Comellas's table, 24 September 2026) becomes a block F_2^3 of 8 points (119 × 8 = 952); each edge of this "controller" graph carries a relation that joins every point to a 2-point affine line of the neighbouring block, following the block-and-line structure of Dharunish Yugeswardeenoo's (12,3) graph on 810 vertices (his table entry of 7 October 2026: a lift over Z_10 with F_3^3 blocks) and Ryosuke Mizuno's route-chart / controller view (arXiv:2606.15860, and his descriptions of the (15,3) 1458 and (16,3) 1920 entries in Comellas's table). In this construction, we add one internal edge per vertex within each block, using the pairing x ↦ x + s_u. This gives degree 6 × 2 + 1 = 13 and allows a controller graph of diameter 3. The relations were found by simulated annealing, shared along a Z_7 automorphism of the 119-vertex graph. Properties: 13-regular, 6188 edges, diameter 3, average distance 2.838127 (version a) and 2.838560 (version b); automorphism group of order 7 with 136 orbits of size 7, as computed using nauty (McKay–Piperno; output included: nauty_952_a.txt, nauty_952_b.txt); the two graphs are not isomorphic (their average distances and distance distributions differ; nauty canonical forms also differ). Verified by separate programs (Python and C breadth-first search) and by F. Comellas's script read70-comp-impl_g6_s6.py run unchanged; the included standalone script verify952.py (plain Python 3) rechecks vertex and edge counts, absence of loops and duplicate edges, degree 13, diameter 3, average distances and the differing distance distributions (output in verify952_output.txt). Files: graph_13_3_n952_a.txt, graph_13_3_n952_b.txt (0-based edge lists "u v", comment on the first line), verify952.py, verify952_output.txt, nauty_952_a.txt, nauty_952_b.txt, SHA256SUMS.txt. AI-assisted (Anthropic's Claude; review of the dataset by OpenAI's ChatGPT) under the author's direction; not reviewed by an outside expert.

Version 4 adds n(5,7) ≥ 5894 (previous lower bound 5824, R. Rajiv, 2026; before that 5516, E. Loz, 2006): a 5-regular
graph of diameter 7 on 5894 vertices, the lift of a 2-vertex voltage graph (a dipole in the sense of Loz and Širáň) over
Z421 ⋊ Z7, product (s,f)(s',f') = (s + 33^f·s' mod 421, f + f' mod 7), a group of odd order 2947. Each vertex type has
two neighbours of its own type and three of the other type. A group of odd order has no involutions, so no Cayley
graph of odd degree exists on it; the two vertex types make an odd degree possible. Automorphism group (nauty) of
order 2947 with two orbits of size 2947, so the graph is not vertex-transitive. Found by simulated annealing on the
voltages in a controlled comparison of odd- and even-order groups, and verified by independent programs (plain-Python
and C breadth-first search from every vertex, NetworkX, F. Comellas's checker: diameter 7, average distance 5.891057).
The search programs were produced with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) under the author's direction;
all results were independently verified.

Version 3 adds two graphs of degree 7:
• n(7,5) ≥ 2758 (previous lower bound 2756, M. J. Dinneen and P. R. Hafner, 1994): a 7-regular graph of diameter 5 on
  2758 vertices, the lift of a 2-vertex voltage graph (a dipole in the sense of Loz and Širáň) over Z197 ⋊ Z7 (order
  1379). Each vertex type has six neighbours of its own type and one of the other type.
• n(7,4) ≥ 684 (previous lower bound 672, M. Sampels, 1997): a 7-regular graph of diameter 4 on 684 vertices, the lift
  of a 2-vertex voltage graph over Z38 ⋊ Z9 (order 342). Each vertex type has four neighbours of its own type and three
  of the other type.
Neither uses an involution (for odd degree a Cayley graph must). Each has an automorphism group of the order of the
lifted group with two orbits, so neither is vertex-transitive. Found by simulated annealing on the voltages over
semidirect products of cyclic groups of order just above half the record, and verified by independent programs
(plain-Python and C breadth-first search from every vertex, NetworkX, F. Comellas's checker). The search programs
were produced with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) under the author's direction; all results were
independently verified.

Version 2 adds n(6,3) ≥ 120 (previous lower bound 119, R. Rajiv, 2026): a 6-regular graph of diameter 3 on 120
vertices, obtained as the lift of a 2-vertex voltage graph over SmallGroup(60,9) ≅ C5 × A4. Each vertex type has one
semi-edge (an involution, i.e. a perfect matching inside the type) and five edges to the other type. Its automorphism
group has order 60 with two orbits of size 60, so it is not vertex-transitive (the Cayley optimum for (6,3) is 108).
It was found by a systematic search over the number of base vertices × all groups of the given order (GAP SmallGroups)
× orders above the record, with simulated annealing on the voltages, and verified by independent programs
(plain-Python BFS from every vertex, a GAP rebuild from the voltages, nauty). Files: edge lists (0- and 1-based),
graph6, construction data, GAP rebuild script, group table, verifier, SHA256SUMS, and a detailed PDF write-up.
The search programs and write-up were produced with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, Anthropic) under the
author's direction; all results were independently verified.

Three graphs that improve the lower bounds in the Table of Large Degree/Diameter Graphs (F. Comellas):
  (Δ,D) = (13,3): order 868   (previous best 859, D. Yugeswardeenoo, 2026)
  (Δ,D) = (14,3): order 1094  (previous best 1088, R. Rajiv, 2026)
  (Δ,D) = (14,4): order 8303  (previous best 8288, R. Rajiv, 2026)

(14,3) order 1094 — an extension of R. Rajiv's 1088-vertex graph. All 7,360 of its edges are kept. Added: 6 new
vertices of degree 14 (80 edges to original vertices, 2 between new vertices) and 215 new edges between original
vertices in their unused degree slots (510 of the 512 unused slots now used). Edge positions found by simulated
annealing until the diameter was 3. Vertices 0–1087 keep Rajiv's numbering (the vertex order of the sparse6 string in his file on the table's site).

(14,4) order 8303 — an extension of R. Rajiv's 8288-vertex graph. All 57,791 of its edges are kept. Added: 15 new
vertices of degree 14 (190 edges to original vertices, 10 between new vertices) and 129 new edges between original
vertices in their unused slots, in two steps (8302, then 8303). Vertices 0–8287 keep Rajiv's numbering (the vertex order of the sparse6 string in his file on the table's site).

(13,3) order 868 — an independent construction. Start from the 585-vertex polarity fold of the generalized
quadrangle over GF(8) (Q'8 family); for each of its 65 absolute vertices add 4 "untied twins" (adjacent to the other
8 vertices of the absolute vertex's line, not to the vertex itself), giving 845 vertices; add a layer of 22 vertices
whose edges, with extra edges in unused slots, are placed by targeted simulated annealing (order 867); then one more
vertex with the annealed edges re-optimised (about 890 of 5,635 edges moved).

Files: plain edge lists, one edge "u v" per line, vertices numbered from 0, first line a comment; SHA256SUMS.txt holds
the SHA-256 fingerprints. Each graph was verified with two independent implementations (breadth-first search from
every vertex, and networkx): maximum degree Δ, diameter D, connected, simple.

The search programs were written and run by an AI assistant (Anthropic's Claude) under the author's direction.
